text: Seek wealth, not money or status. Wealth is having assets that earn while you sleep. Money is how we transfer time and wealth. Status is your place in the social hierarchy.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: The opening of the tweetstorm he posted on 31 May 2018.

text: Understand that ethical wealth creation is possible. If you secretly despise wealth, it will elude you.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: The next tweet in that thread: contempt for wealth is a way of not getting any.

text: You're not going to get rich by renting out your time. You must own equity — a piece of a business — to gain your financial freedom.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: His break with salaried time. Freedom, in this thread, is ownership.

text: Pick an industry where you can play long term games with long term people.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: From the same thread. The returns he cares about compound with the same people.

text: Learn to sell. Learn to build. If you can do both, you will be unstoppable.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: His shortest pairing in the thread: the person who can do both does not have to wait for the other half.

text: Arm yourself with specific knowledge, accountability, and leverage.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: The three tools the rest of the thread unpacks.

text: Specific knowledge is knowledge that you cannot be trained for. If society can train you, it can train someone else, and replace you.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: His test for whether a skill is specific: if a school can stamp it out, the market can swap you.

text: Embrace accountability, and take business risks under your own name. Society will reward you with responsibility, equity, and leverage.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: The thread's bargain: a public name is how judgment gets paid.

text: Code and media are permissionless leverage. They're the leverage behind the newly rich. You can create software and media that works for you while you sleep.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: He sets code and media apart from capital and labor, which someone else has to grant.

text: Leverage is a force multiplier for your judgment.
source: How to Get Rich (without getting lucky)
context: Why he treats judgment as the scarce input once leverage is cheap.

text: Desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want.
context: On The Tim Ferriss Show, 29 October 2015, the line he said he would put on a billboard.

text: A fit body, a calm mind, a house full of love. These things cannot be bought — they must be earned.
context: On the How to Get Rich conversations at nav.al he calls this his favorite tweet: money does not purchase the three things that matter most.
